mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a downturn in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS declines, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in supply-side activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows and corporate earnings are impacted.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO drops > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it signals a potential overheating economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate inflationary pressures and potential monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings are expected to rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 200k and UNRATE drops > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS rises > 200k and UNRATE drops > 0.2pp, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals growing demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as related industries benefit from increased activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST rises > 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to rise.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 rises > 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.
